* Added in the second session
** Guitar voice-led triads
Two guitar voicing styles in voicings.js, both three notes on ONE string set, each chord taking the
shape whose strings move least from the one before (ChordVoicings.lead):
- =triadvl= root-3rd-5th of every chord (a 7th chord gives its plain triad).
- =uppervl= the triad on the 3rd of a 7th chord (3-5-7), 6-R-3 for a 6th chord, b7-9-4 for a 7sus.
The band plays them on strings 4-3-2 up to fret 12 (GUITAR_SETS in harmony.js). The Chord Sheet has a
menu item per string set; a shape picked by hand is kept and the chords after it follow.
Known: through a cycle of fourths (ii-V-I-VI) the nearest shape is always the next one UP, so the
line climbs the neck until it hits fret 12 and jumps back down. That is true voice leading, but it
may not be what is wanted; an alternative is to keep every chord inside one five-fret position.
** Meters
- A beat is the meter's lower note, except in 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8 (compound), where it is the dotted
  quarter: 6/8 has 2 beats, 12/8 has 4, and the tempo counts dotted quarters. BandHarmony.meterInfo
  decides; form bars, ctx and bar records carry =meter= and =compound=.
- In a compound bar x.5 is the beat's THIRD eighth (the player warps it to 2/3); x.333 needs straight:true.
- 3/4: jazz waltz (ride ding, ding-a, ding; hat foot on 2 and 3; kick on 1), bass walks three quarters.
- 6/8, 12/8: every eighth on the cymbal, kick on 1 (and 3), backbeat on 2 (and 4), whatever Feel says
  (the Feel menu is disabled). Bass walks one note per beat with pickup eighths; the riff is a shuffle.
  Comping uses the same figures as 4/4, which land on the triplet grid.
- The page has a Meter menu that re-writes the three blues presets; custom ABC keeps its own M: line.
- Notation writes compound bars in eighths (M:12/8, Q:3/8=); MIDI writes the time signature and
  converts the tempo to quarters.
- NOT done: 5/4, 7/4 and other meters still get the generic four-beat patterns cut to length; 2/2 is
  counted as two half-note beats; no 12/8-specific comping figure (repeated triplet chords); a tune
  that changes between simple and compound meter keeps one tempo number for both kinds of beat.

* Guitar: led by the hand, and two-note chords (2026-10-07, later)
- Guitar shapes used to follow each other by pitch only (ChordVoicings.nearest), which gave the right
  notes on awkward fingerings and hopped string sets. Now ChordVoicings.easiest picks the smallest move
  for the fretting hand: frets the hand shifts + half the fret change on each shared string + 0.75 per
  string picked up or dropped (handMotion); pitch motion only breaks near-ties, with a mild pull to fret 5.
  Used by the band for every guitar style and by the Chord Sheet's "Favor voice leading" on all fretted
  instruments. The weights are first guesses.
- The band remembers the grip it chose; the as-played hand-off carries it ({ strings }) so the Chord
  Sheet draws that fingering instead of the first shape with the same notes.
- =guide2=: two-note chords on string pairs 4-5, 3-4, 2-3 (3rd + 7th/6th; root + 3rd for a triad;
  4th + b7 for 7sus; root + 5th for a power chord). Chord Sheet menu: all pairs, or one pair.
Not done: a pinned voicing from the Chord Sheet has no grip on the band side, so the chord after a pin
is still chosen by pitch; "Standard" guitar shapes on the Backing Track do not exist (Chord Sheet only).

* Moving voicings, bass variation, loop shortcut (2026-10-07, last)
- Voicing movement menu (opts.voiceMove): hold / move / passing. "move" leads comping by the TOP NOTE
  (BandHarmony.toward): a held chord steps through inversions, a chord change continues the line by step,
  turning at the edge of the register. "passing" adds passing diminished chords in the "bh" style.
- Style "bh" (Drop 2, sixth-diminished): each chord read as a sixth chord (BandHarmony.sixthOf): maj -> 6,
  m7 -> 6 a minor 3rd up, dom -> m6 on the 5th (altered: m6 a semitone up), m7b5 -> m6 a minor 3rd up.
- Style "auto": per four-bar phrase from intensity / tempo / rhythm (comp.js autoStyle). With Variation on
  Strict the intensity never moves, so Auto stays on rootless (piano) or shells (guitar).
- "Major 7th chords: play as 6th chords" checkbox (opts.maj6, BandHarmony.asSixth).
- Bass variation follows the Variation menu (opts.variation; 0 = exact): walking skip notes and held notes,
  two-feel 3rds and dotted rhythm, riff relatives (climb, octave, sparse, approach), shuffle approach.
- Loop: L toggles it; first time it starts at the Start bar and the next chart click sets the end. An end
  before the start loops over the end of the form (player.setCycle(9, 1)). Click = end, Shift-click = start.
- Chord Sheet diagrams: fret label 27px in a left gutter, position dots at 3 5 7 9 12 15 17.
All probabilities and weights here are first guesses, unheard.

* Chord Sheet tidy-up and fingerings (2026-10-07)
- Preview bar (Print, Play with the band, notation button) and banjo / mandolin / vihuela are hidden
  by default; two quiet links at the bottom of the page bring them back (localStorage "chordSheetExtras").
- Add by type: one small row, root typed in (C, f#, Bb); the 12 root buttons are gone.
- Solfege, notation and chord-name options moved beside Show fingerings.
- Guitar fingers: one finger per fret from the lowest fretted note, squeezed to fit four fingers;
  barre = 1. Checked against the usual open chords, F and Bm barres, a drop 2 and a shell.
- Piano fingers: scored by natural finger spans (FINGER_SPAN) instead of fixed 1-2-3-5; left hand mirrored.
  Gives RH 135 / 125 / 135 for triad inversions and 1235 / 1245 / 1235 with the octave. LH root position
  with the octave comes out 5-3-2-1 where method books usually print 5-4-2-1.
- Two hands: root position or a low bass note = bass alone in the left hand; rootless or inverted
  four-note chord = two and two.
- Superimposed view (checkbox under the view options): up to four different chords on ONE keyboard
  (a lane per chord, after the Music Will jam cards) and ONE guitar fretboard (a colour per chord, split
  dots where chords share a note). Each chord is voice-led from the one before: nearest inversion on
  the keyboard, easiest hand move on guitar, in whatever voicing style the instrument has selected; the
  first chord is as its ordinary card shows it. Live menus: chord labels (names / Roman / numbers) and
  note labels (fingers / note names / chord tones). More than four chords: a tick row, a fifth tick
  replaces the earliest. A split dot carries one label per slice when the chords disagree (e.g. different
  fingers, chord tones). Covers every keyboard and fretted instrument (guitar, bass, ukulele, ...). Note labels
  also offer solfege (movable do from the key). A voicing picked by hand on a chord's own card (t.manual)
  is kept exactly; chords after it are led from it. Not done: printing.
- Two-hand piano fingering: a lone left-hand bass note is finger 5 and a three-note right hand spans 1 to 5
  (the first version of the span-based fingering printed 1 for the lone note and 1-2-3 for the right hand).
OPEN: bass still shows chord diagrams. Proposed replacement: a chord-tone map (root, 3rd, 5th, 7th as
single notes in one four-fret hand position, fingered) with the arpeggio in bass clef. Needs its own
drawing code because two tones can fall on one string.

* PLAN (steps 1-2 partly built 2026-10-07, see the last round): 9ths, 13ths and alterations, as options
Today: rootless voicings always add a 9th and 13th to a plain 7th chord; shells and guide tones ignore
written extensions; drop 2 / drop 3 keep the four most characteristic tones (C9 -> R-3-7-9, C13 -> 3-7-9-13);
"bh" ignores written 9/13 and only uses alterations to choose its reading; Standard keeps everything.
1. One place for the decision: BandHarmony.colour(chord, policy, nextChord) returning the chord the comping
   voices (as asSixth does now), so every style, the notation and the Chord Sheet agree.
2. Menu "Extensions": As written / Plain (strip to the 7th) / Add 9ths / Add 9ths and 13ths.
   "As written" must really mean it: rootless stops adding 9 and 13 to a bare C7 in that mode.
3. Menu "Dominant alterations": As written / b9 on dominants that resolve to a minor chord / Altered on
   dominants in turnarounds. Needs the next chord (already in ctx.nextChords).
4. Per-style behaviour, written as a table first (C9 C13 C7b9 C7#9 C7#11 C7alt Cmaj9 Cm9 Cm11 C6/9 x style)
   and printed by a test: shells and guide tones gain an optional third "colour" voice (3-7-9, 7-3-13);
   drop 2 gets a choice of which tone gives way (root or 5th); guitar shells put the extension on top;
   two-note chords stay 3rd and 7th.
5. "bh" readings for extended chords are a musical decision to make together: G9 is already Dm6; G13 and
   G7#11 have more than one accepted reading.
6. With colour on, the top-note line prefers the extension. The bass scale must follow added alterations
   (no natural 9th in the line under a b9).
7. The same two menus on the Chord Sheet, so its diagrams match what the band plays.

* Half time / double time (opts.timeFeel = "normal" | "half" | "double")
- BandHarmony.feelPart(part) wraps each part; BandPlayer and BandMidi.generate wrap every part with it and pass
  ctx.form / ctx.nextIndex. The chart, tempo, bar count, loop, stops and highlight are untouched: only what the
  part is shown (chords re-placed on a beat half or twice as long, tempo scaled) and where its events land.
  Events come back already swung at the part's own tempo, marked straight:true.
- Half time pairs bars by form index (1+2, 3+4...). An odd last bar, or starting / looping from the second bar
  of a pair, still works: the wrapper generates the whole pair and keeps the half it needs.
- Who changes: opts.timeFeelParts ("bass drums" by default, "drums", or "bass comp drums"). User correction:
  the comping does not double just because the rhythm section does, so it is left out unless asked for.
- Pinned voicings are re-keyed onto the wrapped bar numbers (pinsFor), so they are used in every mode.
- Limits: off in compound meters (6/8, 12/8); stop bars are played in normal time; wrapped comp events lose
  their `of` key so the hand-off to Chord Sheet re-voices; written-out notation of pre-swung sixteenths may
  look rough (unchecked).
- Odd-length bars in half time (3/4, 5/8, 7/8): the bar line falls in the middle of a band beat, so the second
  bar's chord is placed one chart beat EARLY (a push). Delaying it was the alternative.
- PINNED (user: "put a pin in it"): grouped meters. 5/8 and 7/8 are still counted as five / seven equal beats.
  Half time gets part of the way (two bars of 5/8 = one bar of five quarters, half as many notes), but a
  single bar felt 3+2 needs beats of unequal length, the way 6/8 already has beats of three eighths. Also
  pinned with it: force straight feel in x/8 meters, MIDI export writes 5/8 as 5/4.
- Idea not built: per-part time feel (drums in half time under a normal bass), and a time feel per style
  (the "Pop ballad" style's Half-time drum groove is really this).

* Intros (player cfg.intro / player.setIntro)
- { bars, kind: "vamp" | "last", tacet: "drums" }: bars played once after the count-in, only when play starts
  from bar 1. The parts get ordinary bar contexts (index 0..n-1, chorus 0, intro:true), so a tune's bass line
  or two-bar pattern runs through the intro. Stops and pins do not apply. Not in the bar log, so "export what
  was played" and the written-out chorus leave it out; a fresh MIDI export has no intro either.
- Page: Intro / Intro length / "Drums wait for bar 1" in the Play panel, saved with a setup. Loading plain
  changes, or a setup that does not mention them, clears intro, time feel, figure and stops.
- Song for My Father: four bars of Fm, bass figure + piano (its bossa pattern, NOT doubling the bass figure
  as on the record), drums in at the top. Length from the user (2026-10-07).
- Built with the anacrusis in mind: the intro is a play-once list of bars ahead of the form (Session.intro).
  A pickup would be one more (short) bar at the end of that list; rule still to write: the intro's last bar
  leaves room for it. The short LAST bar that balances a pickup is separate.
- Not built: an intro with its own chords; other parts sitting out; a drum fill into the top.
